  fields[z]=ndi.distance_transform_edt(m)-ndi.distance_transform_edt(~m)
 zs=sorted(polys)
 xx,yy=np.ogrid[:512,:512]
 for z in range(zs[0],zs[-1]+1):
  if z in fields:f=fields[z]
  else:
   zl=max(v for v in zs if v<z);zh=min(v for v in zs if v>z);t=(z-zl)/(zh-zl);f=fields[zl]*(1-t)+fields[zh]*t

# Paired CT lesion analysis

The best-effort masks identify **one confluent retroperitoneal lesion in each examination** (local ID 1). Its left para-aortic, retro-aortic and interaortocaval portions are connected and are therefore represented as one instance. The matching location relative to the aorta, vena cava, vertebrae and renal vessels supports a **persistent** correspondence. This describes identity, not stable size. No other definite tumor focus was identified in the volume review.

Both complete input volumes were reviewed in axial soft-tissue views, with supplementary lung-window views and targeted coronal/sagittal reformats. Image-guided native axial contours were interpolated using signed distance fields, then refined with intensity-based vessel/fat exclusions and visual overlay checks. No external data or pretrained models were used. The outputs are uint16 masks on the original grids; shape, affine, qform and sform equality and complete event-ID coverage were verified.

| Input file | Local ID | Labeled native axial slices, inclusive | Approximate mask volume |

Localization and correspondence are more certain than the exact boundary. I’m now reviewing both at matched world positions in soft-tissue and lung windows so findings aren’t missed because of slice-index or field-of-view differences.

The dominant suspicious finding is a large irregular enhancing breast mass that is present at both visits and appears smaller later. I have not found a convincing abdominal/pelvic tumor on the full-volume review so far; I’m checking the breast lesion’s exact 3D boundaries and separately reviewing axillary/internal mammary nodes and the lungs before finalizing the lesion count.

The obvious rounded opacity at the right lung base proved to be the hepatic dome/diaphragmatic contour rather than a lung lesion, and the large posterolateral soft tissues are symmetric shoulder/axillary muscles. I’m using the scanner affines to resample the later exam onto the earlier grid and review subtraction/fused views; this is mainly to expose subtle interval lesions that side-by-side viewing can miss.
